# MeTTa from C

A C11 program embeds SWI, builds owned atoms, runs MeTTa and publishes native
callbacks. No CPython runtime is required. C atoms are materialized values;
SWI term handles never escape their foreign frame. The engine defines the
language semantics, and kit/corpus.json compares this seat with live pymetta.

## Build and install

Run `sh build.sh` and `sh test.sh` in this directory. SWI development headers
and a C11 compiler are required. Tests stage a private engine fixture under
ai-tmp. Set METTA_PATH to the engine tree when using an isolated checkout.

`make install PREFIX=/your/prefix` installs the header, engine and
libcmetta.so.1. Obtain consumer flags with `pkg-config --cflags --libs cmetta`.
`make install-check` builds and runs a consumer of that installed interface.
MIGRATION.md describes the ABI 1 changes.

## A program

```c
#include <cmetta.h>
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    metta *m = mt_open(NULL);
    if (!m) { fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", mt_errmsg()); return 1; }
    mt_each (a, mt_run(m, "(= (double $x) (* 2 $x)) !(double 21)"))
        printf("%s\n", mt_show(a)); /* 42 */
    int failed = !mt_ok();
    mt_close(m);
    return failed;
}
```

One context is exposed per process. Repeated mt_open calls with the same
configuration return it; they are not independent owners. Named spaces
separate source and storage but share native registrations. The application
coordinates the single mt_close.

## Atoms and ownership

A `const mt_atom *` parameter borrows; a mutable atom parameter transfers one
reference. Constructors return owned atoms. Accessors borrow from their parent.
Use `mt_keep` to transfer another reference and `mt_drop` to release one.

```c
mt_atom *fact = mt_expr("edge", "alice", mt_var("who")); /* (edge alice $who) */
mt_add(m, mt_keep(fact));                             /* retains fact here */
mt_drop(fact);
```

A bare C string in a term is a symbol; `mt_text` constructs text.
`mt_sym` and `mt_def` preserve exact spelling. A registration named word_count
is called word_count. Names never acquire another identity in the binding.

`mt_atom_of` and `mt_expr` dispatch on C types. Unsigned values preserve all
64 bits. Booleans need `mt_bool`; C integer promotion otherwise gives them
integer meaning. Use `mt_exprv` for arrays and arbitrary arity; the convenience
variadic macro accepts up to sixteen children. `MT_SHORTHAND` enables
`S V T N R B E` builders.

Kinds are MT_SYMBOL, MT_VARIABLE, MT_EXPR, MT_TEXT, MT_BOOL, MT_INT, MT_FLOAT,
MT_BIGINT, MT_RATIONAL, MT_SPACE, MT_OBJECT and MT_HANDLE. `mt_kind_of(NULL)`
returns MT_NONE. `mt_int` requires an exact int64 value; `mt_float` refuses
lossy integer conversion. `mt_unum` preserves uint64 and `mt_bigint`
canonicalizes decimal spelling, folding values that fit to MT_INT.

`mt_eq` and `mt_hash` compare structure. Hashes include process-local object
identity and must not be persistent IDs. `mt_unify` and `mt_unifyv` borrow
their inputs and return owned bindings; a mismatch is NULL without an error.
Use `mt_binding`, `mt_binding_var`, `mt_binding_value`, `mt_bindings_len`
and `mt_substitute`, then `mt_bindings_free`.

Atom construction, inspection, unification and destruction need no engine.
`mt_parse` reads one form, `mt_parsen` reads counted source, and `mt_forms`
returns an owned list of all forms without executing directives. A later
syntax error returns no prefix. These readers require an open runtime.
`mt_show` is rotating presentation text; `mt_show_dup` returns owned text.
`mt_write_dup` returns counted, reader-inverse `mt_string` data or refuses a
value without a source spelling. Release owned strings with `mt_free`.

## Caller memory

`mt_allocator_set((mt_allocator){resize, user})` selects a per-thread
realloc-shaped allocator and returns the previous selection. Sizes include
the private ownership header; a failed growth preserves the old block.
Allocate transferred list arrays with `mt_alloc` or `mt_calloc`, resize
through `mt_resize`, and release through `mt_free`. Never pass these blocks
to libc free, or libc blocks to mt_free. Existing blocks keep their allocator,
whose callback and user must outlive them and support cross-thread release.
SWI retains ownership of its own heap.

`mt_text_ref(bytes, length, owner, release)` borrows immutable bytes with a
trailing NUL. `mt_expr_ref(count, children, owner, release)` borrows an
immutable child vector and retains each child. `mt_children` returns the
vector directly. These constructors allocate only the atom descriptor and
take the owner's release obligation only on success. Engine transport still
converts the atom. mt_drop uses no allocation and no recursive calls.

## Spaces, source and answers

`mt_space_open(m, "&kb")` returns an owned C handle; close it with
`mt_space_close`. `mt_self` and `mt_catalog` borrow runtime-owned handles.
`mt_space_drop` retires the engine space and declarations without freeing the
C handle. Obtain an anonymous space through the engine's new-space operation.

The generic verbs `mt_run`, `mt_load`, `mt_do`, `mt_eval`, `mt_match`,
`mt_atoms`, `mt_add`, `mt_add_all`, `mt_del`, `mt_count` and `mt_wipe`
accept a runtime or a space. Source runs in the receiver's module. mt_run
and mt_load are eager; `mt_do` discards their answers. `mt_forms` only parses.
mt_del removes one unifying occurrence and refuses a bare variable; MeTTa's
remove-atom drains a pattern. mt_add_all takes its list array and atoms.

Outside a closed transaction, mt_eval pulls incrementally. `mt_step(r, &a)`
returns MT_ROW, MT_DONE or an error and borrows the current atom until the
next step. `mt_next` is its pointer form; `mt_answers_status` preserves the
terminal status. `mt_each` closes on break or exhaustion. Use explicit
`mt_answers_free` for return/goto paths, or the compiler's `MT_AUTO_ASK`.

`mt_rows` exposes `mt_row` with atom, text, group and cursor. Group identifies
the source directive. `mt_bound(row, "x")` borrows a match binding.
Multiplicity is preserved; result order within a group is not promised.

`mt_one` requires exactly one answer; `mt_first` takes the first and closes
the rest; `mt_all` returns an owned `mt_list`. All consume the cursor.
mt_one and mt_all discard a collected prefix if a later pull fails. Free
collections with `mt_list_free`.

## Native producers and function values

`mt_iterator {state, next, close}` is the C generator protocol. next returns
MT_ROW with an owned atom, MT_DONE with NULL, or an error. close runs once.
`mt_answers_from` consumes an iterator on every path, even failure.

Register `mt_op {.name, .arity, .effect, .fn, .user}` through `mt_def`.
The callback reads `mt_arg`, returns `mt_answer` for one atom,
`mt_answer_iter` for a producer, or `mt_fail` with a reason. Producer
arguments stay alive until close. Declare MT_NONDET or a stronger effect for
a producer. The effect vocabulary also includes MT_PURE, MT_LOOKUP, MT_WRITES
and MT_IO; `mt_effect_str` gives the engine spelling.

`mt_object(pointer, type_name, release)` carries one opaque identity. Its exact
type_name also reaches the engine's get-type and typed dispatch; NULL supplies
no type candidate. The engine performs type inference.
Wrap once and retain it when aliases must be identical; independent boxes
are independent ownership identities. `mt_function(fn, user, release)`
carries an applicable function value. Both take their resource even when
construction fails. `mt_value` and `mt_type` borrow the C payload and name.
`mt_object_free` consumes an atom and invalidates engine aliases immediately;
otherwise the final C and engine owners determine release.

A producer returned by a function value is an opaque iterator. Consume it
with `(c-iter ($f ...))`, or use `mt_stream_of` to borrow its C cursor.
`mt_stream` constructs such a value directly. These streams are consumptive.

## Lowering

`mt_lower(m, (twice $x), (* 2 $x))` installs an inspectable equation from
preprocessor tokens. `mt_lower_raw` and `MT_METTA_RAW` preserve tokens
without expanding colliding C macros. Parameterizing a body by its operators
can emit both C and MeTTa; examples/lower.c runs that construction. Arbitrary
compiled machine code has no recoverable C AST. $ identifiers require the
GCC/Clang extension; use source strings on another compiler.

## Transactions and events

`mt_transaction(m, callback, user)` commits MT_OK, rolls back MT_FAIL,
and rolls back error statuses with their original reason. `mt_speculate`
always discards. Nested scopes are savepoints; engine state and C
registrations share the verdict. C memory and I/O need their own recovery.
Enter every enclosing transaction through C before changing registrations from
a callback. A raw nested engine transaction cannot own a C registry snapshot.

Queries opened inside a closed scope collect through the engine's held
cursor service. Commit retains their answers; rollback discards them. Bound
an unbounded producer before opening it there: SWI cannot yield across a
transaction goal.

`mt_subscribe(m, name, subscription)` takes an `mt_subscription` containing
space, owned pattern, notify callback, user and release. It watches both
committed additions and removals; notify borrows the atom and receives true
for an addition. Return MT_OK or an error. Rollback delivers nothing.
A callback error reports after commit and does not undo it.
`mt_unsubscribe` cancels; self-cancellation retains data until notify returns.
The subscription owns its name-based lifetime: cancel before reusing the
watched space name. The caller owns queues and scheduling.

## Queries, cells, types and algebras

`mt_query(space, pattern, guard)` consumes both atoms and opens the engine term
`(match space pattern (if guard pattern Empty))`. A NULL guard means True.
Conjunction patterns express joins. Build a prepared query once, pass mt_keep
at each call, and it reads current facts. Add temporary facts inside
mt_speculate and collect answers with mt_all before leaving the callback.

Use engine terms new-state, get-state and change-state! for mutable cells.
The current engine rolls cell writes back with the surrounding transaction.
Type declarations and get-type express typed atoms and array shape relations.
A C buffer remains a C resource; it acquires no inferred engine schema.

`mt_eval_under(space, algebra, goal)` consumes both atoms and returns an owned
cursor of ordinary `(value coefficient)` pairs from the engine's annotation
service. The algebra is queryable engine data, scoped to that evaluation.
Compose reads with a match over `(superpose (space-a space-b))`.

Owned mt_all lists are snapshots. Incrementally maintained answers, reified
world orchestration, saga receipts and tagged proof reinterpretation currently
live in the Python surface. They need shared engine services before C can
expose equivalent operations without duplicating language semantics.

## Providers and extensions

`mt_provider` passes borrowed atoms directly to add/remove and opens a
candidate iterator through match. A variable pattern requests enumeration.
The engine unifies each candidate; duplicates remain duplicate answers.
The match limit is advisory and may be ignored. Apply it only to exact
answers. NULL callbacks decline capabilities. remove reports whether one
occurrence was removed through its bool output.

Supply begin/commit/rollback together or omit all three. Completion retains
the chosen provider across withdrawal and name reuse. Queries retain it
through close. `mt_provider_open` takes user on every path;
`mt_provider_close` releases the name.

`mt_extension` loads a shared object exporting `mt_extension_init`.
Initialization runs transactionally over C registrations and engine state.
`mt_library` registers source paths and `mt_repr` registers display callbacks.
`mt_point_declare`, `mt_register`, `mt_unregister`, `mt_point_of`,
`mt_point_at`, `mt_point_count`, `mt_seam_at`, `mt_seam_count` and
`mt_claim` expose the extension registry as data. Libraries can declare their
own points. The core does not guess array or table schemas from void pointers.

## Errors, bounds and threads

Errors are per-thread and errno-shaped: set on failure, not cleared on success.
Use `mt_clear` before a checked region, then `mt_ok`, `mt_error` and
`mt_errmsg`. `mt_remedy` and `mt_ground` return the engine's refusal advice
when supplied. Callbacks can set a typed error with `mt_error_set`.

`mt_limit` bounds evaluation and reports MT_LIMIT. The inference budget is
cumulative for a lazy cursor; the wall bound applies to each pull.
`mt_stats_now` and `mt_stats_since` measure a region.
Other threads call `mt_thread_attach` and `mt_thread_detach`.
Immutable atoms may be shared; cursors and callback state need caller
serialization. Publish and withdraw registrations while evaluation workers
are quiescent. Notification callbacks run on the writer's thread.

cmetta.h is the complete contract. README.md gives worked examples and
MIGRATION.md the ownership changes.
